key_insight: KNIGHT combines topic-specific knowledge graphs with LLM prompting to automatically generate high-quality multiple-choice questions and uses adaptive hardness calibration to control difficulty for robust evaluation of retrieval-augmented systems.
problem_solved: Reduces the time, cost, and manual effort of building specialized MCQ evaluation datasets for LLMs and RAG systems while improving factual grounding and controllable difficulty.
method: Construct a compact, topic-specific knowledge graph from external sources to provide structured, factual context.
Prompt an LLM to generate question stems, answer keys, and plausible distractors grounded in the KG.
Apply an adaptive hardness calibration module that adjusts distractor selection and question phrasing to produce target difficulty levels.
impact: Enables scalable, cost-effective creation of grounded MCQ datasets with tunable difficulty, improving benchmarking and stress-testing of LLMs and RAG pipelines for researchers and practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data source → knowledge graph construction → LLM question + distractor generation → adaptive hardness calibration → MCQ dataset
Annotated MCQ example: show source KG facts, question stem, correct answer, and distractors with notes on grounding and hardness
Difficulty calibration chart: distribution of easy/medium/hard questions before and after calibration (bar or violin plot)
Evaluation summary: small bar chart comparing model performance on KNIGHT-generated vs. manually created MCQs
paper_title: KNIGHT: Knowledge Graph-Driven Multiple-Choice Question Generation with Adaptive Hardness Calibration
paper_authors: Mohammad Amanlou, Erfan Shafiee Moghaddam, Yasaman Amou Jafari, Mahdi Noori, Farhan Farsi
